newsitem.title: UK: Man Utd shares drop to five-month low.
newsitem.headline: Man Utd shares drop to five-month low.

text.p: Shares in Manchester United Plc dropped to a near-five month low on Friday as end-of-season lethargy continued to weigh on the leading soccer stock, dealers said.
The stock was down 16-1/2p at 605p by 1324 GMT, after earlier dropping as low as 587p -- some 10.6 percent below its level at the end of last week.
Despite clinching the English soccer championship this week for the fourth time in the past five years, Manchester United shares have dropped sharply in the past three sessions.
"It is just profit-taking with nothing to go for until the start of the new season," said one market-maker in the stock.

Manchester United shares powered to a record 737p in January, driven by hopes for continued success on the pitch and prospects for lucrative pay-per-view television revenues with the launch of multi-channel digital services.
The club's soaring market value helped inspire a rush of English clubs onto the market, with Aston Villa Plc -- up 45p at 995 in thin volume of 1,150 shares -- most recent to join.
Yet some dealers cast doubt on the scale of revenues that clubs will make from pay-per-view television.
"I just wonder if people will cough up when they are asked to pay for individual matches," said one.
Among other top soccer stocks, Newcastle United Plc was up 1/2p at 119-1/2 and Chelsea Village Plc was down 1p at 126-1/2.
